title: Buffer Solutions and Titrations - Chemistry - Henderson–Hasselbalch Equation
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Select the correct form of the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for a weak acid ($$ \text{HA} $$) and its conjugate base ($$ \text{A}^- $$).
questions.explain: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation is derived from the $$ K_a $$ expression and is written as: $$ \text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log \left( \frac{[\text{base}]}{[\text{acid}]} \right) $$. For a weak acid/conjugate base pair, this is $$ \text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log \left( \frac{[\text{A}^-]}{[\text{HA}]} \right) $$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the pH of a buffer solution where the concentration of the weak acid ($$ \text{HA} $$) is equal to the concentration of its conjugate base ($$ \text{A}^- $$)?
questions.explain: According to the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: $$ \text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log \left( \frac{[\text{A}^-]}{[\text{HA}]} \right) $$. If $$ [\text{A}^-] = [\text{HA}] $$, then the ratio is 1, and $$ \log(1) = 0 $$. Therefore, $$ \text{pH} = \text{p}K_a $$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Calculate the pH of a buffer solution containing $$ 0.10\,\text{M} $$ acetic acid and $$ 0.10\,\text{M} $$ sodium acetate. Given: $$ K_a $$ for acetic acid is $$ 1.8 \times 10^{-5} $$.
questions.explain: First, calculate $$ \text{p}K_a = -\log(1.8 \times 10^{-5}) \approx 4.74 $$. Since the concentrations of acid and base are equal ($$ 0.10\,\text{M} $$ each), $$ \text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log(1) = 4.74 + 0 = 4.74 $$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: A buffer solution contains $$ 0.50\,\text{M} $$ ​$$ \text{HA} $$ ($$ \text{p}K_a = 5.0 $$) and $$ 0.50\,\text{M} $$ ​$$ \text{A}^- $$. If $$ 0.01\,\text{mol} $$ of solid NaOH is added to $$ 1.0\,\text{L} $$ of this buffer (assuming negligible volume change), what is the new pH?
questions.explain:
Initial moles: $$ \text{HA} = 0.50 $$, $$ \text{A}^- = 0.50 $$. Added NaOH ($$ 0.01\,\text{mol} $$) reacts with HA: $$ \text{HA} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{A}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} $$. 
New moles HA = $$ 0.50 - 0.01 = 0.49 $$. 
New moles $$ \text{A}^- $$ = $$ 0.50 + 0.01 = 0.51 $$. 
$$ \text{pH} = 5.0 + \log(0.51/0.49) \approx 5.0 + 0.017 = 5.017 \approx 5.02 $$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: You need to prepare a buffer with pH 5.00 using an acid with $$ \text{p}K_a = 4.70 $$. What ratio of $$ [\text{A}^-]/[\text{HA}] $$ is required?

questions.q: What is the effective pH range of a buffer usually considered to be relative to its $$ \text{p}K_a $$?
questions.explain: A buffer is generally effective when the ratio of base to acid is between 1:10 and 10:1. This corresponds to a pH range of $$ \text{p}K_a - 1 $$ to $$ \text{p}K_a + 1 $$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Under which condition does the Henderson-Hasselbalch approximation fail to accurately predict pH?
options: When the concentrations of acid and base are equal.
When the acid or base concentrations are extremely dilute or the $$ K_a $$ is relatively strong (approaching $$ 10^{-2} $$).
When the solution is at room temperature.
questions.explain: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation assumes that the dissociation of the weak acid is negligible and that water autoionization is negligible. These assumptions break down for relatively strong 'weak' acids or extremely dilute solutions.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Calculate the pH of a buffer solution composed of $$ 0.20\,\text{M} $$ ammonia ($$ \text{NH}_3 $$) and $$ 0.20\,\text{M} $$ ammonium chloride ($$ \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} $$). $$ K_b $$ for $$ \text{NH}_3 $$ is $$ 1.8 \times 10^{-5} $$.
questions.explain:
First, find $$ \text{p}K_b = -\log(1.8 \times 10^{-5}) = 4.74 $$. 
Using the basic form: $$ \text{pOH} = \text{p}K_b + \log([\text{salt}]/[\text{base}]) = 4.74 + \log(1) = 4.74 $$. 
Then, $$ \text{pH} = 14.00 - \text{pOH} = 14.00 - 4.74 = 9.26 $$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What mass of sodium acetate ($$ \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} $$, molar mass = 82 g/mol) must be added to 1.0 L of 0.10 M acetic acid ($$ \text{p}K_a = 4.74 $$) to produce a buffer of pH 4.74? (Assume no volume change)
questions.explain:
Since the target pH (4.74) equals the $$ \text{p}K_a $$ (4.74), the ratio of $$ [\text{A}^-] $$ to $$ [\text{HA}] $$ must be 1. 
Thus, $$ [\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}] $$ must equal $$ [\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}] = 0.10\,\text{M} $$. 
Moles needed = $$ 0.10\,\text{mol}/\text{L} \times 1.0\,\text{L} = 0.10\,\text{mol} $$. 
Mass = $$ 0.10\,\text{mol} \times 82\,\text{g/mol} = 8.2\,\text{g} $$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
